current_findings.classification: source-established conditional owner-recovery risk; no observed loss or runtime validation
current_findings.first_contract: An anonymous browser is issued a random owner and attempts durable starting-character creation before the cookie bearing the only presented token is returned. On a create call error the route returns without it; a successfully committed create whose HTTP response never arrives also leaves the browser without it.
current_findings.conditions: Assume an anonymous first creation actually commits but its create-call completion is reported as an error, or the final response carrying Set-Cookie is lost. The same candidate retry with a freshly issued different owner is rejected by the claim guard. Random owner collision is not ruled out mathematically. No native transport completion semantics, client retry, transaction atomicity, recovery flow or actual player state was inspected or probed.
current_findings.safeguards: Success and selection-failure paths explicitly attach the token after the grant; existing validated sessions retain their owner. Owner guards deliberately prevent transfer. Do not claim every create error committed or every session is orphaned.
current_findings.relationship: Related to q529 owner-key representation and q530 entropy failure, but a different conditional issuance/commit/delivery contract; not automatically an alias of either.
current_findings.future_repair_direction: After the audit gate, design an established, recoverable browser identity and explicit ambiguous-completion retry policy before creating an exclusive owner-bound claim; preserve owner exclusivity and legitimate error semantics. No implementation proposed here.

current_findings.classification: source-established conditional valid-content loss; no observed catalog occurrence or runtime validation
current_findings.first_contract: Validated authored interpretation accepts at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes. The native deduction producer adds the 25-byte prefix learned diagnostic clue: and retains the result; the web projection silently filters every item longer than 1,024 bytes. Consequently valid 1,000–1,024-byte interpretations become 1,025–1,049-byte entries and are filtered under the stated chain.
current_findings.conditions: An author supplies an otherwise valid 1,000–1,024-byte nonempty interpretation; the diagnostic is successfully learned and a matching report generates the merged deduction that reaches this owner-scoped web projection. The arithmetic counts UTF-8 bytes, not characters. No actual catalog item of that length, completed transaction, UI observation, product build or runtime execution was established.
current_findings.relationship: q539 is a separate first failure for malformed JSON defaulting to empty; the prior L05 evidence-knowledge provenance issue concerns different producers/identity. Same field or word is not proof of a duplicate. Central reconciliation owns final identity.
current_findings.future_repair_direction: After the audit gate, align length admission with the actual final provenance representation or retain structured bounded components; preserve valid content, owner privacy, legitimate empty lists and distinctions between malformed and absent data.

current_findings.classification: current elaboration of historical Adler environmental question; conditional, not an observed incident
current_findings.first_contract: unix_seconds converts a pre-epoch SystemTime error to zero. A token issued while the clock is before epoch is timestamped zero; if subsequently verified at an ordinary modern date it is past the 30-day lifetime and is rejected.
current_findings.conditions: Requires a pre-epoch host clock at issuance, durable grant, later restored modern clock and use of that cookie. No such environment or grant was observed; supported clock policy, durable token recovery and native clock behavior remain open.
current_findings.relationship: Adler READ-L11-386 already identified the pre-epoch-zero environmental policy question. Preserve that attribution; do not invent a separate historical finding or automatically equate this clock cause with lost HTTP delivery.
current_findings.future_repair_direction: Resolve clock-error and identity lifetime policy with the identity recovery contract after the audit gate.

lens_notes.producer_propagation: Trace issued token and owner through creation/grant/cookie; trace bounded Bestiary interpretation through receipt, deduction, projection and web presentation. Other producers and consumers remain open.
lens_notes.type_ownership: q529 asks owner identity placement across issuance/grant; provenance length ownership is split between authoring, producer and projection. No shared crate owner is selected here.
lens_notes.type_granularity: Distinguish token, owner identity, candidate request key, granted character, diagnostic text and rendered provenance. Some are strings at boundaries; q529 and conditional length case need shared semantic decisions.
lens_notes.admission_contracts: 32-byte token ID, signature and expiry checked; native owner format and grant relationship checked; q196 admits unexpected known-tag payload; 1,024-byte upstream component and final item admission mismatch.
lens_notes.invariant_operations: SystemTime error defaults to zero, later expiry can reject token under clock-fault condition. Prefix operation increases the UTF-8 byte length before fixed-cap filtering.
lens_notes.enum_shapes: q196 single-key representation drops payload; unknown variant names reject. Grant provenance uses origin plus two Options and validates matching arm, but no mutation bypass is shown in inspected support.
lens_notes.aggregate_states: Issuance, durable claim, delivery and exclusive owner are a cross-step lifecycle; no transaction/transport semantics inferred. Current grant provenance arm validation is present.
lens_notes.magic_numbers: Session ID=32 bytes, expiry=30 days, skew=5 minutes and provenance limit=1,024 have visible roles; whether their values and policy ownership are correct remains open. The prefix costs 25 bytes.
lens_notes.magic_strings: Versioned session cookie and owner domain mark protocols; generated owner keys and candidate request keys remain strings, with validation/format described. No broad literal-to-type claim is made.
lens_notes.existing_type_owners: GrantedCharacterId encapsulates u64 within session; owner key lacks a shared bespoke boundary (q529). Existing owner inventory outside registered support is unresolved.
lens_notes.redundant_authority: Session ID derives owner hash; claim and grant both contain owner and are explicitly checked. De-duplication or competing authorities are not established; delivery recovery is the separate lifecycle question.
lens_notes.behavior_preservation: Retain legitimate empty provenance, owner secrecy, successful idempotent same-owner retry, grant exclusivity and selection-failure cookie path when future repairs are considered; no runtime behavior validated.
lens_notes.derivability: Derives on simple wrappers are source observations; cryptographic/token admission and conditional deserialization are semantic, so no boilerplate removal is established in this bounded scope.

limitations.evidence_only: Read-only Git objects, source inspection, recovery, JSON/gzip parsing and hash verification only. No product edits, builds, tests, browser, runtime probes, simulations or shaders.
limitations.publication: Central agent alone owns authoritative baseline, cross-lens identity, ledger and checkpoint publication. Historical or reconstructed evidence is not promoted into checkpoint3821.
